history.summary: Spacious 1484sqft 3BR at $1273 psf, ~18% under the Quartz median of $1550, just 270m from Buangkok MRT in a large 625-unit GuocoLand development. Sub-$1.9M price and MRT-adjacency give it broad resale appeal; 6.38%/yr appreciation on 120 transactions is healthy. Reviews are mixed on interior materials and facility upkeep.
history.rating_rationale: Strong value-plus-location: ~18% below development median, $1.89M in the liquid HDB-upgrader band, and a genuine 3-minute (270m) walk to Buangkok MRT — the best MRT proximity in the D19 group after La Fiesta. 6.38%/yr resale CAGR on 120 txns is solid. Build quality is the watch-item: reviews call interior materials low-class and note dated/dirty facilities for the age. Not a frontier unit (record 563-4-2) but a clean, sensible buy.

history.summary: A jumbo 2,906 sqft unit in Sengkang (D19) asking $1,032 psf vs a verified ~$1,495 psf project average — a large nominal discount, but it is a size artefact: jumbo units structurally trade far lower psf, the algo has ZERO same-size comparables, and the ~$3M quantum on a 99-yr (2005) lease has narrow exit liquidity.
history.rating_rationale: Web-verified recent Quartz transactions average ~$1,495 psf (range $1,417-$1,584), so the $1,032 psf headline looks like a ~31% bargain and drives the algo's -35.7% age-adj signal and the 'very_low_psf' flag. But psf_cohort_txns=0 — there is no same-size band to compare against, so the -32.2% vs-cohort number is a data quirk, exactly the trap to be skeptical of. This is a 2,906 sqft jumbo (a comparable jumbo is asking $3.3M), and giant units always carry a deep psf discount versus the regular-sized units that set the $1,495 average — so the discount is largely mechanical, not free value. Lease is 99-yr from 2005 (~78 yrs left, built 2009). Catalyst is limited to existing Buangkok/Hougang MRT. For a 5-7yr investment, the ~$3M quantum + jumbo format means a small buyer pool and slow exit; the abundant space is a feature mainly for own-stay, not investment. Net: fairly priced for what it is, but not an investment bargain — Neutral.
